title: Atomicity, isolation and server-side validation
objection: Redis has no transactions, so you cannot maintain invariants.

claims.claim: MULTI/EXEC does NOT roll back: 1 command failed, yet 'before'=1 and 'after'=1 both applied
claims.detail: This is the objection, and it is correct. MULTI is batching + isolation, not a transaction. Do not build invariants on it.

claims.claim: read-modify-write corrupts the store under contention: 69 invariant violations (13 index mismatches, 12 runs in wrong number of indexes, 44 lost version bumps)
claims.detail: This is what people actually ship, and it is the real source of "Redis lost my data" stories.

claims.claim: WATCH/MULTI/EXEC holds the invariants: 0 violations, at the cost of 285 retries
claims.detail: optimistic concurrency works, but 72.0% of attempts had to be redone — that is wasted work that grows with contention

claims.claim: Lua holds the invariants with zero retries: 0 violations, 0 retries
claims.detail: the script is the unit of atomicity; no other command interleaves, so there is nothing to retry

claims.claim: Lua p99 latency 11.315 ms vs WATCH 23.458 ms
claims.detail: fewer round trips and no retry loop

claims.claim: a client asking for succeeded→running is refused server-side (returned 0); run stayed 'succeeded'
claims.detail: the legality table lives in the script, so no client version, no retry loop and no rogue service can write an illegal state

claims.claim: the same procedure loaded as a Redis Function library and executed via FCALL (returned 1)
claims.detail: Functions persist in the RDB/AOF and replicate to replicas — server-side logic becomes part of the database, not of whichever client happens to connect
